raw_case_text:
A 26-year-old man with a past medical history of unspecified hepatomegaly at birth, and alcohol use disorder since he was 20 years of age, went to the Emergency Department complaining of 5 days of throbbing headache, arthralgias, myalgias, and a documented fever (40.4 C) that partially improves with ibuprofen and with no response to paracetamol.
The clinical course was exacerbated on day 2 of the initiation of symptoms by crampy (colicky) abdominal pain in the epigastrium with radiation to the right upper quadrant, accompanied by nausea and vomiting.
Admission physical exam revealed blood pressure (BP) of 120/90 mmHg, heart rate (HR) of 56 bpm, respiratory rate (RR) of 20 rpm, oxygen saturation of 97% in room air, and temperature of 36.6 C. Disseminated petechiae were observed on the patient's face, trunk, and extremities. Cardiac and lung exams revealed normal heart sounds, without rhythm alterations, no murmurs, and lung fields were clear, without wheezing, rhonchi, rales, or crepitus. Examination of the abdomen revealed scattered petechiae, increased abdominal perimeter (95 centimetres), tenderness to palpation in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant, without hepatosplenomegaly, and no guarding or rebound tenderness. Bowel sounds were present. The pulses in the extremities were regular, and there was no edema.
Laboratory tests (Table 1) performed on the patient's hospital admission revealed a hematocrit of 49%, platelet count of 23.000, C-reactive protein (CRP) of 29.2, glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) of 747 U/L, glutamic pyruvic transaminase (GPT) of 509 U/L, amylase of 229 U/L, lipase of 258 U/L, gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) of 604 U/L, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) of 208 U/L, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) of 995 U/L, and lactic acid of 3.4 mmol/l, triglycerides of 267 mg/dl, cholesterol of 158 mg/dl, mild hypophosphatemia of 2.4 mg/dl, and albumin of 3.7 g/dl and glucose of 112 mg/dl.
Ultrasonography of the abdomen revealed an enlarged liver, with increased diffuse echogenicity and reinforcement of the periportal vessels, homogeneous structure, and fluid at the level of the left hepatic border that extended to Morrison's space. Gallbladder with walls of normal thickness, without endoluminal images, nondilated bile ducts, slightly hypoechoic pancreas, preserved shape and structure, and scant perisplenic fluid, slight bilateral pleural effusion associated with a consolidation process with air bronchogram was also seen.
Having ruled out the biliary cause of pancreatitis and searching for other causes, there were no calcium abnormalities, hypertriglyceridemia, endocrine abnormalities, or use of drugs associated with pancreatitis. Due to a history of fever and being a resident of an endemic area of the dengue virus, a viral panel was requested, resulting in positive IgM and IgG antibodies for dengue, with negative NS1 antigen (Table 2), qualifying it as dengue with warning signs.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old male presenting with high fever (40.4 °C), throbbing headache, arthralgia, and myalgia for five days, with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for three days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 26-year-old male presented with a 5-day history of throbbing headache, arthralgias, myalgias, and high fever (40.4 °C) partially responsive to ibuprofen and unresponsive to paracetamol. On illness day 2, he developed severe crampy epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Hospital evaluation revealed acute pancreatitis and acute hepatitis alongside petechial rash and hemoconcentration.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unspecified hepatomegaly at birth; alcohol use disorder since age 20. Resident of a tropical arbovirus-endemic area.
subjective.review_of_systems: Crampy epigastric and right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting; absence of hematemesis or melena.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 36.6 °C, blood pressure 120/90 mmHg, heart rate 56 beats/min (bradycardia), respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, SpO2 97% on room air. Dermatologic: Disseminated petechiae over face, trunk, and extremities. Cardiopulmonary: Normal heart sounds, lungs clear bilaterally without crackles or wheezing. Abdomen: Increased abdominal girth (95 cm), scattered petechiae, exquisite tenderness to palpation in epigastrium and right upper quadrant, without hepatosplenomegaly, guarding, or rebound tenderness; normal bowel sounds. Extremities: Peripheral pulses regular, no peripheral edema.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: Hematocrit 49% (hemoconcentration), platelet count 23,000/microL, CRP 29.2 mg/L, GOT/AST 747 U/L, GPT/ALT 509 U/L, amylase 229 U/L, lipase 258 U/L, GGT 604 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 208 U/L, LDH 995 U/L, lactic acid 3.4 mmol/L, triglycerides 267 mg/dL, cholesterol 158 mg/dL, serum phosphorus 2.4 mg/dL, albumin 3.7 g/dL, glucose 112 mg/dL. Abdominal and thoracic ultrasound: Enlarged liver with increased diffuse echogenicity and periportal cuffing/vessel reinforcement; free fluid along the left hepatic border extending to Morison's pouch; gallbladder of normal wall thickness without gallstones; non-dilated intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts; slightly hypoechoic pancreas with preserved parenchymal shape; scant perisplenic fluid; mild bilateral pleural effusions with consolidation and air bronchograms.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Confirmed Dengue virus infection (dengue with warning signs and severe plasma leakage) complicated by acute pancreatitis (elevated lipase and amylase), acute hepatitis, and polyserositis (ascites and bilateral pleural effusions). Confirmed by positive Dengue IgM and IgG antibodies by viral panel (with negative NS1 antigen). Biliary obstruction, choledocholithiasis, severe hypertriglyceridemia, hypercalcemia, drug-induced pancreatitis, and alcoholic pancreatitis etiologies were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Inpatient admission for guided intravenous fluid resuscitation, multimodal analgesia, pancreatic rest, gastroprotection, and close monitoring of hematological and hemodynamic parameters.
